title: Slack Pro to self-hosted Rocket.Chat
summary: Rocket.Chat is the closest thing to Slack you can run yourself, and seats are where Slack's bill compounds.

you_lose: Slack's 2,600-app directory and the integrations your team already installed
Huddles and clip — the low-friction audio/video that keeps people out of meetings
Someone else handling the next security patch on a chat server that faces the internet
you_gain: No per-seat charge, so guests and whole departments stop costing money per head
Unlimited message history — the Free-tier 90-day limit and the Pro-tier pins both go away
Matrix federation and an API you can automate against without approval

caveats: Rocket.Chat's community edition carries most of the product, but some features (LDAP, audit, OAuth enterprise) are enterprise-licensed — check your must-haves against their edition matrix before committing.
Chat history grows fast. The 40 GB backup assumption fits a chatty 12-person team for about two years; re-check if you migrate years of logs in.
Migration means re-creating channels and re-inviting people — Slack does not export member relationships to a competitor. The 10-hour estimate is for a 12-seat workspace, not a 200-seat one.
